_purpose: GH-403. The ten development sites' real nutrition-programme INPUTS, so the effect of removing nutrition-calendar.js's whole-kilogram rounding of the annual requirement can be measured before and after, on every site, offline. tests/gh403-required-one-quantity.test.js loads nutrition-calendar.js twice — once as it stands, once from a copy with that one line put back — and runs both over these inputs, so 'what moved' is measured against the old code rather than transcribed.
_source: docker exec gilba_mysql mysql -ugilba: site_configs.config.nutritionCalendarProgram for every site in namespace 'gaip', read 2026-09-10. Each site's block below is that persisted programme's own inputs, read back off it: meta (species, methodology, surface, hemisphere, distribution, annual N base, clipping, traffic), soil (ppm, bulkDensity, soilDepth), adjustments (traffic modifier, monthly N cap), the twelve monthly temperatures, and the RESOLVED sufficiency ranges (annual_totals_range + its per-nutrient source). Test5 - NZ's tissuePercent comes from its tissue sample, samples.id=144 (N 4.57 / P 0.62 / K 2).
_whyRangesArePassedIn: Supplying `ranges` bypasses nutrition-program-inputs.js's resolver, which needs pH / CEC / texture from the sample. The ranges recorded here are the ones the live run actually resolved, so the replay uses the site's real floors and ceilings without depending on three sites whose soil samples are no longer in the dev database. nutrition-requirement-core.js reads `ph` only to stash it, never to compute, once ranges are given.
_notAnExpectedBlock: `persisted` is the programme the live run WROTE, kept for orientation, and is deliberately not asserted equal to the replay. The stored monthly temperatures are rounded to 1 dp by computeProgram() itself, so replaying from them moves GP by up to 0.01 and a monthly row by up to 0.1 — and three of these programmes (Canberra, Russley, test4 - USA) were generated before GH-398/400 and would not reproduce under today's code anyway. What the test asserts is the BEFORE/AFTER difference on one set of inputs, which that noise cannot manufacture: both runs see the same inputs.
